description: Consolidated map of every rendering-related asset the original engine touches: shaders (custom and third-party), fonts, UI/portrait/icon images, and 3D model sources vs. their compiled cache form. Cross-references world_assets.json (model catalogue) and game_assets.json (fonts/audio/render settings).

keyFinding_mediaTreeFound.summary: UPDATE: the source media tree IS present in this workspace, at top-level 'media/' (sibling of jCRPG-engine/, jCRPG-engine's own code expects it one level up as '../media/' when run from jCRPG-engine/). It contains real, plain-text/plain-image source assets for everything the engine renders: raw .obj/.mtl/.3ds models, all quality tiers of texture, UI art, character portraits, icons, shaders, audio, fonts, and — critically — the scenario's default_worldparams.xml and default_ecology.xml (see worlds.json, updated).

topLevelLayout.media/models/<category>: raw Wavefront .obj + .mtl source meshes (bush, external, fauna, grass, ground, humanoid, inside, item, monster, tree) — same categories as world_assets.json, 86 .obj files total
topLevelLayout.media/sides/: top-level (not under models/) .3ds/.obj/.mtl source for space.sidetype Cube face geometry (maze walls/ground, cactus, etc.)
topLevelLayout.media/textures/models/{common,low,low_pn: per-quality-tier texture sets for the models above (154 files at medium/high/low)
topLevelLayout.media/textures/{cursor,flare,icons,orbit: cursor art, lens flare, item/state/entity icons (textures/icons/{objects,states,entities}), sun/moon orbiter textures, and a 6-side skybox (day/ and night/ variants)
topLevelLayout.media/ui/: 102 files — window frames, HUD, meters, dice, hourglass, plus subfolders busy/, windowicons/, popups/, inventory/, mapicons/, mainmenu/, topbuttons/, characters/
topLevelLayout.media/portraits/{human,elf,dwarf,catkind: character portrait art (112 human, 26 dwarf, 15 elf, 4 catkind files) — confirmed to directly match starter_party.json pictureId values (e.g. ELMO's 'francesco_hayez1.png' exists under portraits/human/male/, ELMARA/PALMANO's portraits under portraits/elf/)
topLevelLayout.media/font/: conc_font/font/vinquefont source art backing the in-repo vinque.fnt+png
topLevelLayout.media/shaders/: bbGrass/fader/grassMove vertex-billboard grass shaders plus a shaders/xray/ subfolder, distinct from the custom DOF/shadow/normalmap shaders already cataloged below under jCRPG-engine/src/main/resources
topLevelLayout.media/ai/ecology/default_ecology.xml: the REAL bestiary/population placement rules (see worlds.json)

keyFinding_mediaTreeFound.implication: Real textures, UI art, portraits, and now the actual scenario data files are all available in this repo. The web port can use these directly (after format conversion where needed, e.g. .dds -> .png/.webp) instead of authoring placeholder art.

modelCacheFormatCorrection.note: jCRPG-engine/cache/*.obj are NOT plain-text Wavefront OBJ despite the extension. Verified by inspection: each cache file is gzip-compressed and decompresses to a binary Ardor3D 'BinaryExporter' scene-graph dump (serialized Spatial/TextureState/ColorRGBA/etc.). The REAL plain-text .obj sources live in media/models/** (e.g. media/models/bush/Bush_01.obj: 90 vertices, 144 uvs, 36 faces, confirmed via 'file' and grep) and are what the cache was generated from.
modelCacheFormatCorrection.producedBy: org.jcrpg.apps.BinaryConverter: ObjImporter loads a real .obj from ../media/**, builds an Ardor3D Spatial, then BinaryExporter.save() serializes the whole scenegraph (geometry + material/texture state) which is written to cache/<TEXDIR>/<flattened-path>.obj and is gzip-compressed on disk.
modelCacheFormatCorrection.namingConvention: Cache filename = the source file's path relative to '../media/' with '/' replaced by '_', extension kept as .obj. E.g. cache 'models_external_House_01_wall.obj' <- source 'media/models/external/House_01_wall.obj'; cache 'sides_maze_wall_thick.obj' <- source 'media/sides/maze_wall_thick.obj' (top-level 'sides' tree, not under 'models').
webPortImplication: Use media/models/**/*.obj (+ matching .mtl) directly as the real mesh source for the web port — no need to reverse-engineer the Ardor3D binary cache format at all.
Load via three.js OBJLoader/MTLLoader (or pre-convert to glTF offline for smaller/faster-loading files); texture references in the .mtl files should be repointed at media/textures/models/<quality>/.

families.description: Multi-pass depth-of-field: render depth buffer (1_depth / 1_depth_nv variants for nvidia-specific depth fetch), gaussian blur (2_gauss), then combine near/far blur with sharp focus (3_dof variants) into a fullscreen composite.
Custom project-space shadow mapping shader (distinct from Ardor3D's bundled PSSM shadow shaders below; used by the older jME2-based render path).

Per-pixel normal mapping and parallax-mapping variants (plain + point-light variants) used for detailed ground/wall/model surfaces; referenced in code as 'org/jcrpg/threed/jme/effects/shader/normalmap/parallax'.

A full screen-space ambient occlusion pipeline (pre-render depth pass, SSAO pass + a 'cSSAO' cone/color variant, separable X/Y blur, final texturing composite). Present in the resource tree but not confirmed wired into an active Java render pass in the packages searched — likely an experimental/unused feature.

sourceInMedia.description: Billboard grass movement/wind-sway shaders (bbGrass*/grassMove*) and a screen fader, plus an xray/ variant set. Separate from the compiled custom shaders bundled into jCRPG-engine/src/main/resources above (those look like build output of these or a related source tree; both are now available for direct comparison/reuse).

bundledInLibraries.description: Real GLSL shader source text bundled directly inside the third-party jars in jCRPG-engine/lib/ (plain resource files inside the jar's zip structure — extractable with a plain unzip, no decompilation needed).

families.description: Flat vs. projected-grid water, each with a plain and a refraction-enabled variant; WaterRenderPass.simpleShaderStr/projectedShaderStr pick which pair loads at runtime.
Bright-pass extract -> separable gaussian blur (5/7/9-tap horizontal+vertical variants, with a downsampled vertical5 pass) -> final additive composite.

families.javaOwner: com.ardor3d.extension.shadow.map (used by the newer Ardor3D-based render path)
families.description: Parallel-Split Shadow Maps (cascaded shadow maps) plus a debug-visualization variant.
Geometry clipmap terrain LOD rendering (with a specular variant) plus a generic texture-clipmap shader used for large splatted ground textures.

families.javaOwner: not directly referenced under org.jcrpg.* in this codebase search — likely unused (engine primarily uses billboard/rigid models, see world_assets.json)
families.description: GPU vertex-skinning shaders for skeletal animation, part of the ardor3d-animation extension the game depends on but may not exercise for its (mostly static/billboard) creature and humanoid models.

families.javaOwner: legacy jME2 render path (superseded by Ardor3D pssm shaders above)
families.description: Old jME2 shadow-map shader, kept only because jme.jar is still a dependency; not the shader family actually driving current SHADOWS behavior (that's the in-repo custom shadowMap.* or Ardor3D pssm.*).

webPort.approach: Port each family to WebGL2/GLSL ES via three.js ShaderMaterial/RawShaderMaterial: water and bloom map almost 1:1 to common three.js postprocessing passes (three/examples/jsm/postprocessing); PSSM shadows can be replaced wholesale by three.js's built-in CSM (cascaded shadow maps) support; DOF and SSAO likewise have off-the-shelf three.js passes and don't need the original GLSL ported verbatim.

customInRepo.format: BMFont (Angel Code) — .fnt descriptor + glyph atlas PNG
customInRepo.usage: The game's actual in-scene UI/HUD text font.

bundledFallback.usage: Ardor3D's own default UI text font; present as a library fallback, not the game's chosen font.

legacy.usage: jME2's built-in default font texture; leftover from the older render path, not used by the current UI (which uses vinque).

fonts.webPort: Convert vinque.fnt/png (or re-render at higher res from media/font/ source) to a standard BMFont-compatible web renderer, or use it as an MSDF font source.

uiAndPortraitImages.status: Present in this workspace at top-level media/ (see keyFinding_mediaTreeFound above)
